_about: Key markets, restaurants, bars, cafés and sights in São Paulo. Coordinates are approximate (typically within 100–200 m) and are replaced by Google's exact location when a Google Places key is configured. Ratings always come from Google, never from this file.

places.name: Mercado Municipal de São Paulo (Mercadão)
places.notes: The big one: 1933 market hall with stained glass. Mortadella sandwich at Hocca Bar, pastel de bacalhau at Bar do Mané, fruit stalls upstairs (agree a price before tasting).

places.name: Mercado Municipal Kinjo Yamato
places.notes: Wholesale-style fruit and veg market behind the Mercadão, in the Zona Cerealista of grain, spice and nut shops along Rua Santa Rosa.

places.name: Rua 25 de Março
places.notes: Latin America's biggest open-air shopping street: cheap clothes, fabrics, party goods, electronics. Very crowded; keep valuables close.

places.name: Mercado Municipal de Pinheiros
places.notes: Smaller, foodie-focused market near Largo da Batata: Amazonian ingredients at Comidinhas de Dona Onça, oysters, craft beer, good lunch counters.

places.name: Feira da Benedito Calixto
places.notes: Antiques, vintage clothes, records and crafts on Praça Benedito Calixto, with live chorinho music in the afternoon.

places.name: Feira da Liberdade
places.notes: Japanese and Chinese street food (yakisoba, tempura, gyoza) and crafts on Praça da Liberdade in the Japanese quarter.

places.name: Feira do Bixiga
places.notes: Flea and antiques market on Praça Dom Orione in the old Italian quarter; cantinas and pizzerias all around.

places.name: Feira de Antiguidades do MASP
places.notes: Antiques fair under the museum's famous red span on Avenida Paulista, which is closed to cars on Sundays.

places.name: Feira de Artesanato da República
places.notes: Crafts, gemstones, food stalls and street performers on Praça da República.

places.name: Feira Orgânica do Parque da Água Branca
places.notes: Organic producers' market in a leafy park; good for fruit, cheese and breakfast pastel.

places.name: CEAGESP Varejão
places.notes: Brazil's largest produce terminal. The public retail sessions sell fruit, veg, flowers and fish at wholesale prices.

places.name: Mercado Municipal da Lapa
places.notes: Neighbourhood market from 1954 with butchers, cheese stalls and a few lunch counters; quieter than the Mercadão.

places.name: Mercado Municipal de Santo Amaro
places.notes: Southern-zone market with a good food court; the fried-fish and pastel stalls are the draw.

places.name: Casa Santa Luzia
places.notes: Upmarket deli and grocer since 1926: Brazilian cheeses, cachaças and sweets to take home.

places.name: A Casa do Porco
places.notes: Jefferson and Janaína Rueda's pork temple, regularly in the World's 50 Best. Long queues; the tasting menu or the porco San Zé. Book ahead.

places.name: Bar da Dona Onça
places.notes: Janaína Rueda's bar-restaurant at the foot of the Copan building: feijoada, coxinha, caipirinhas.

places.name: D.O.M.
places.notes: Alex Atala's two-Michelin-star tasting menu built on Amazonian ingredients. Reserve well ahead.

places.name: Maní
places.notes: Helena Rizzo's relaxed fine dining in a garden house; famous for the 'ovo perfeito' and the weekend lunch.

places.name: Padoca do Maní
places.notes: Maní's bakery next door: sourdough, pão de queijo, coffee and a cheaper way to taste the kitchen.

places.name: Mocotó
places.notes: Rodrigo Oliveira's sertanejo cooking: dadinhos de tapioca, carne de sol, cachaça list. Worth the trip north; no bookings, go early.

places.name: Figueira Rubaiyat
places.notes: Steak and seafood under a giant 100-year-old fig tree. Dinner under the tree is the point.

places.name: Jiquitaia
places.notes: Marcelo Corrêa Bastos's homage to Brazilian home cooking; excellent-value lunch menu.

places.name: Evvai
places.notes: Luiz Filipe Souza's Michelin-starred tasting menu mixing Italian technique with Brazilian produce.

places.name: Metzi
places.notes: Modern Mexican tasting menu using Brazilian corn; one of the city's most talked-about tables.

places.name: Nelita
places.notes: Tássia Magalhães's handmade pasta and Brazilian seasonal plates; lively counter seating.

places.name: Arturito
places.notes: Paola Carosella's wood-fired cooking in a converted house; set lunch is good value.

places.name: Balaio IMS
places.notes: Rodrigo Oliveira's downtown outpost inside the IMS cultural centre on Avenida Paulista: great lunch between museums.

places.name: Komah
places.notes: Paulo Shin's Korean food with Brazilian ingredients; bibimbap and the pork belly.

places.name: Bráz Pizzaria (Moema)
places.notes: São Paulo-style pizza done properly: thin crust, generous toppings. Try the Bráz with zucchini.

places.name: Pizzaria Speranza
places.notes: Classic Bixiga pizzeria since 1958; margherita and the calabresa are the standards.

places.name: Hocca Bar (Mercadão)
places.notes: Home of the famous mortadella sandwich (ask for it with provolone). Share one; it is enormous.

places.name: Bar do Mané (Mercadão)
places.notes: The other Mercadão institution: pastel de bacalhau (salt-cod pastry) and cold beer.

places.name: Famiglia Mancini
places.notes: Theatrical old-school cantina on Rua Avanhandava with a huge antipasti bar. Expect a wait.

places.name: Cantina Jardim de Napoli
places.notes: Famous for the polpettone alla parmigiana since 1949.

places.name: Z Deli Sandwiches
places.notes: Pastrami on rye and the Reuben; a good quick lunch between Jardins shops.

places.name: Tordesilhas
places.notes: Mara Salles's long-running tour of regional Brazilian cooking: moquecas, tutu de feijão, Saturday feijoada.

places.name: Lanchonete da Cidade
places.notes: Retro lanchonete with good burgers, milkshakes and the baked pastel.

places.name: Jun Sakamoto
places.notes: Tiny counter and one of Brazil's most respected sushi chefs. Book the counter seats.

places.name: Tan Tan Noodle Bar
places.notes: Ramen, dumplings and inventive cocktails; listed among Latin America's best bars.

places.name: Jamile
places.notes: Henrique Fogaça's lighter restaurant: wood-fired lamb, hummus and vegetables.

places.name: Corrutela
places.notes: Zero-waste kitchen milling its own flour; short, seasonal menu.

places.name: Vista Ibirapuera
places.notes: Rooftop of the MAC museum with a view over Ibirapuera Park; strong on seafood and Brazilian flavours.

places.name: Rinconcito Peruano
places.notes: Cheap, authentic Peruvian: ceviche, lomo saltado, chicha morada.

places.name: Frevo
places.notes: Since 1956 on Oscar Freire: the beirute sandwich and a draft chope.

places.name: Estadão Bar e Lanches
places.notes: Open 24 hours; the pernil (roast pork) sandwich is the late-night classic.

places.name: Ponto Chic
places.notes: Birthplace of the bauru sandwich in 1934.

places.name: Veloso Bar
places.notes: Arguably the city's best coxinha and caipirinhas; arrive before it opens to beat the queue.

places.name: Bar Brahma
places.notes: 1948 bar on the famous corner from the Caetano Veloso song; samba and chorinho nightly.

places.name: Bar Léo
places.notes: Since 1940, draft beer poured properly and bolinho de bacalhau.

places.name: Bar Original
places.notes: Famous for perfectly poured chope and the pastel de carne.

places.name: SubAstor
places.notes: Speakeasy below Bar Astor; one of Latin America's 50 Best Bars.

places.name: Guarita Bar
places.notes: Small, creative cocktail bar led by Jessica Sanchez.

places.name: Bar dos Arcos
places.notes: Cocktails in the brick arches beneath the Theatro Municipal.

places.name: Bar Pirajá
places.notes: Rio-style boteco with a good chope and petiscos; busy after work.

places.name: Terraço Itália
places.notes: 41st-floor view over the whole city; come for a sunset drink rather than dinner.

places.name: Coffee Lab
places.notes: Isabela Raposeiras's roastery-café; Brazilian single-origin tastings.

places.name: KOF – King of the Fork
places.notes: Serious third-wave coffee from Brazilian farms, plus brunch.

places.name: Café Girondino
places.notes: Belle-époque café by the São Bento monastery; coffee, chope and a pastel between downtown walks.

places.name: Casa Mathilde
places.notes: Pastéis de nata and other Portuguese sweets in a grand old-bank setting.

places.name: MASP – Museu de Arte de São Paulo
places.notes: Lina Bo Bardi's red concrete span; strong European collection on glass easels.

places.name: Parque Ibirapuera
places.notes: The city's main park with Niemeyer buildings, museums and the Japanese pavilion.

places.name: Pinacoteca de São Paulo
places.notes: Brazilian art in a beautifully converted 1900 building next to Jardim da Luz.

places.name: Beco do Batman
places.notes: Ever-changing graffiti alley; bars and galleries around it.

places.name: Edifício Copan
places.notes: Niemeyer's curving 1960s residential block; rooftop visits at set times, bars at street level.

places.name: Theatro Municipal
places.notes: 1911 opera house; guided tours and cheap concert tickets.

places.name: Catedral da Sé
places.notes: Neo-Gothic cathedral at the symbolic centre of the city (the Marco Zero is in front).

places.name: Farol Santander
places.notes: Art-deco skyscraper with a 26th-floor viewing deck and exhibitions.

places.name: Mosteiro de São Bento
places.notes: Benedictine monastery with Gregorian chant at Sunday Mass and a bakery selling the monks' bread.

places.name: Museu do Futebol (Pacaembu)
places.notes: Football museum inside the Pacaembu stadium.

places.name: Japan House São Paulo
places.notes: Kengo Kuma-designed Japanese cultural centre on Paulista; free exhibitions.
